acceptable_changes: 'Earl Russell suited him' became 'suited the Minister' to avoid misreading 'him' as the son.
'If they were not satisfied with Congress, they were satisfied' became 'But the secretaries were satisfied', because Congress is no longer introduced.
'All a secretary could hope to gain' was recapitalized after its preceding clause was removed.
'its practical value' was recapitalized as 'Its practical value' to begin a sentence.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: V1, the droll likeness, the act-as-though-false stance, 'senile from youth' and the November 12 confusion all remain. 'him' became 'the Minister' because the next antecedent is now the son. 'Yet after' became 'After'.
cut_evaluation.reason: Removed the 'played his hand' sentence, the October 1862 betrayal counterfactual, the idee fixe sentence and 'They had never got beyond 1815.'

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: The imperial flush, the vertigo, power taking shape behind the chaos and 'The student could only study' carry the essential spring 1863 function.
cut_evaluation.reason: Cut the 'campaign more beautiful' sentence, the twenty-five-years and stars sentence, and 'Men seemed to have learned their business'.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: V3, Delane's eye, the clause naming the Times's satirical leader on the Manchester letter, and the 'whole generation' close remain. The not-thinking-of-himself turn is kept.
cut_evaluation.reason: Cut the opening sentence about slow Englishmen and gloating, 'Delane probably regarded it as a piece of Milnes's foolery', and the 'British mind is the slowest' sentence.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: The weakly-manned Legation sentence stays to state thin staffing. The opening of paragraph 7, 'If they were not satisfied with Congress', would have been orphaned because Congress no longer appears. It was repaired to 'But the secretaries were satisfied with Secretary Seward.'
cut_evaluation.reason: This follows the plan to condense the staffing grievance. The three-secretary sentence, 'A great staff would have suppressed him' and the volunteer sentence were cut.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: The copied notes and the measuring of men's motive forces remain. These still set up the 'measuring the men' line in paragraph 13.
cut_evaluation.reason: Removed 'No more volunteer services were needed;' because the volunteer setup was cut.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: The secrecy is restated in the retrospect in paragraph 14 ('burying in profound secrecy'). The loss of hope, the raising of tone and V5 remain.
cut_evaluation.reason: Removed the sentence on Russell's still-secret hostile activity of 1862.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: 'Its' refers back to the battle. The respect for traditional England, North and Canning, the boy's idea, the Government's idea and 'jaws of war' all remain.
cut_evaluation.reason: Cut the 'never again find education to compare' clause and kept its second half as 'Its practical value as education...'.

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: The dates 1866, 1878 and 1889 still mark the biography clearly as the later source.
cut_evaluation.reason: Removed 'Not until long after Earl Russell's death was the question reopened.'

cut_evaluation.dependency_check: These carry the essential retrospect argument and the date continuity of 1, 3, 5 and 8 September.
cut_evaluation.reason: Rejected further cuts in the evidence sequence: the Gotha callback, 'incredible grossness', the 3 September letter, Palmerston's purchase suggestion, the tardy notice and the Bravay/Turks letter.
The 'one or two' setup must sit immediately before V8.

review_focus: The transition from paragraph 6 (weakly-manned Legation) to paragraph 7 ('But the secretaries were satisfied').
'Its practical value as education' in paragraph 13: check that the antecedent (the battle) reads clearly.
Paragraph 5: Delane 'had never heard of young Adams' now follows directly on the eye contact.
risks: The estimated reduction runs slightly beyond 303 words, but the code count has not been taken. The final length may fall a little under or over 2300.
The loss of the British-mind aphorism and the stars-on-collars sentence thins some characteristic texture.
summary: Cut an estimated 300-plus words, mostly as whole optional sentences, from the father-and-son opening, the spring 1863 reverie, the Milnes scene's framing, the staffing passage, the 'this is war' lead-in and the 1889 retrospect. Protected excerpts, performed documents, the date sequence and the Gladstone 'one or two' close are unchanged. Small repairs were made only where a cut left a pronoun or reference without a clear referent. The final length has not been measured.
